summary: Thailand grants visa-free entry of up to 60 days to passport holders of 93 countries and territories, runs a single global eVisa portal for everyone else, and requires all foreign arrivals to submit the Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) before travel.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on the date of arrival.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: An International Certificate of Vaccination (ICVP) for yellow fever is required only if you arrive from, or transited through, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

source.name: Department of Disease Control, Thai Ministry of Public Health

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not mandatory for visa-exempt tourists, but medical coverage is strongly recommended — public hospitals require payment from foreigners.

source.name: Department of Consular Affairs, Thai MFA

onwardTicket.text: Immigration officers and airlines may ask for proof of onward or return travel within your permitted stay.

source.name: Department of Consular Affairs, Thai MFA

proofOfFunds.text: You may be asked to show adequate finances: 20,000 THB per person (40,000 THB per family) in cash or equivalent.

source.name: Department of Consular Affairs, Thai MFA

declarations.name: Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC)
declarations.text: All foreign nationals arriving in Thailand must submit the Thailand Digital Arrival Card online before entry. It is free. Use only the official immigration website.

currencyLimits.text: Foreign currency of 20,000 USD or more (or equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure. Taking more than 50,000 THB out of the country requires declaration.

notes: Duty-free allowance: 200 cigarettes and 1 liter of alcohol per adult.
E-cigarettes and vaping devices are prohibited — possession can lead to fines or arrest.

payments.text: Cards are accepted in hotels, malls and larger restaurants; markets, street food and taxis are cash-first. QR payments (PromptPay) dominate locally but usually require a Thai bank account.

safety.text: Thailand is generally safe for visitors. Exercise normal precautions; petty scams target tourists in major cities, and extra caution is advised in the far southern border provinces.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Thailand Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to February is the cool, dry season — the most comfortable time across most of the country.

idp.text: Thailand is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either.

driving.text: Thailand is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Thailand yet.

tips.text: Overstaying costs 500 THB per day (capped at 20,000 THB); overstays of 90+ days trigger multi-year re-entry bans.
E-cigarettes are illegal to bring into or use in Thailand.
Thailand has strict lèse-majesté laws — never comment disrespectfully on the monarchy, online or offline.
The TDAC arrival card is free. Third-party websites charging a fee for it are unnecessary. Use only tdac.immigration.go.th.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Thailand?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders can enter Thailand visa-free for up to 60 days, extendable once by 30 days at an immigration office. They must still submit the free Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) before travel.

faq.question: What is the TDAC and who needs it?
faq.answer: The Thailand Digital Arrival Card is a free online arrival form that every foreign national must submit within 3 days before arriving in Thailand, at tdac.immigration.go.th. It replaced the paper TM6 card.

faq.question: How much does a Thailand tourist visa cost?
faq.answer: For nationalities that need one, the single-entry tourist visa costs about 40 USD and the 6-month multiple-entry visa (METV) about 200 USD, applied for at the official portal thaievisa.go.th. Most Western and many Asian passports do not need a tourist visa for stays up to 60 days.

faq.question: Can I extend my visa-free stay in Thailand?
faq.answer: Yes. Visa-exempt visitors can apply once for a 30-day extension at any Thai immigration office for a 1,900 THB fee, bringing the total stay to up to 90 days.

faq.question: Is travel insurance mandatory for Thailand?
faq.answer: No, insurance is not an entry requirement for tourists, but medical treatment must be paid for, so cover is strongly recommended.
